title: Native Clifford realization of the P104 low-rank channel (no new kappa)
body:
PR1972 supplies a complete P104 `G/2` channel with arbitrary dirty helpers, but its replay assumes abstract consistent frame charts. This adds a concrete finite native realization at its pinned head `fd82d172f46933fd253c2c6de4bd5eaff5429cfd`: 740 exact Clifford transport recipes, 208 monomial intrinsic endpoint adapters, and a separate checker for the complete 280-input framed composition. The scalar channel and schedule remain credited to their authors.

The compiler first converts compressed E8 labels through their actual Gram form into physical binary labels. Independent signed-Pauli and exact Gaussian interpretation checks every primitive, including global phase, and all 4096 private-drop basis columns. The complete row induction restores all 72 arbitrary dirty helpers. Five genuine mutations reject. The profile remains **rank mass 2368 = boundary coverage 2312 + COPY56**.

**No new kappa or complete P104 supplier.** The `I-G/2` side correction, chronological global ownership, recursive precision and all-size admission remain open. The selected record is unchanged. This closes a finite native-realization obligation, not those later gates.

Validation at `6e222517e182e98499239bc9a4009f540e1c5520`:

- Local Python 3.11.15 and 3.14.8 receipts are byte-identical; a read-only relocated export also passes complete recipe regeneration.
- Linux CI: [all three jobs pass](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38597630611) on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.14, including complete regeneration. All three downloaded receipts are byte-identical to the local receipts.
- Standard-library, read-only replay: `python3 -I -O -B research/p104-native-channel/verify.py --regenerate`. Regeneration uses temporary storage and compares complete decompressed payloads. Registered package metadata and source pins pass.

Credit Rohan Arun / [PR1972](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1972) for the entire scalar/frame channel, Adam Gall / [PR1940](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1940) for the schedule, Josie Elliston / PR1071 for the fixture, Ali Romman / PR1125 and PR1862, and the retained E8, dirty-helper and exact-compiler lineage. Exact input pins and inherited notices are included. Native lowering and independent checker work prepared for Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review or formal proof assistant.
